finalText:
Redis died at `02:14:07` and never came back. All good before that: normal traffic, cache hit ratio 0.98.

The moment redis dropped, `api` fell back to hitting the store directly for every request. That caused a cache miss storm, and the store couldn't keep up, so requests started timing out after 5000ms. Redis kept trying to reconnect every ~80 seconds, 13 times, all refused, right up to the crash.

With the store overloaded, the request queue kept growing, from 52 up past 560, never draining. `worker-2` finally ran out of memory holding the backlog and crashed at `02:31:44`. The supervisor restarted it, but eight seconds later `api` also stopped responding, so the whole process group was killed and the service went down.

So: root cause was redis at `10.0.0.12:6379` going unreachable at `02:14:07` and staying down. Everything after was 17 minutes of cascading backlog until the crash at `02:31:52`. Fixing this means getting redis back up and probably capping the queue so a dead cache can't take the whole service down next time.
